title: Platform — outbox and messaging
description: The two lanes of §9.4, kept apart. §13.6: the lanes fail for different reasons, produce different symptoms and need different people — a single averaged 'outbox backlog' panel is one nobody can act on. Broker-lane stalls are Platform's, local-lane stalls and abandoned rows are the service team's (§13.8).

panels.title: Lane age — has a lane STOPPED
Broker lane — oldest unprocessed (alert: 2 min)
panels.description: Other services are working from stale data and sagas stop advancing. The threshold is an order of magnitude above the local lane's because this one crosses a network and should absorb a short RabbitMQ blip or a rolling restart. Runbook: docs/runbooks/outbox-broker.md

panels.title: Local lane — oldest unprocessed (alert: 30 s)
panels.description: Read models this service feeds from its OWN events are stale. Not the ones another service's contract feeds — those never touch this lane, and §13.7 records that their staleness has no direct signal yet. Runbook: docs/runbooks/projection-lag.md

panels.title: Depth — is a lane FALLING BEHIND
Pending rows, per lane (alert: >1000 and rising)
panels.description: Neither gauge substitutes for the other. A single stuck row pins the age panel above at hours while this one stays at 1, and a backlog of ten thousand rows all seconds old leaves the age panel flat. Runbook: docs/runbooks/outbox-growth.md

panels.title: Abandoned rows, per lane (alert: >0)
panels.description: Permanent data loss. A row past §9.4's attempt cap is skipped for ever. IT STAYS COUNTED AS PENDING and keeps the age panel up, so the panels to the left do NOT go green — this looks exactly like an ordinary stall there, which is why this gauge exists: it separates a row nothing will retry from one that is merely waiting. The lane says whose loss: Broker, and other services never learned something; Local, and this service's read model is permanently wrong. Runbook: docs/runbooks/outbox-abandoned.md

panels.title: Event end-to-end p95 (target 2 s)
panels.description: messaging.delivery.lag — OccurredAt to consumer start. IT DOES NOT COVER BROKER-FED READ MODELS: IntegrationEventConsumer<T> records this at the top of Consume, BEFORE it resolves a handler, so the measurement stops where the projection starts. This panel can sit inside its target while ordering.ProductPrices is stale or was never written. §13.7 records that gap as owed.

panels.title: Read-model staleness, own events, p99 (target 1 s)
panels.description: projection.lag is recorded by ProjectionInvoker after a registered IProjectionHandler<T> succeeds — Ordering's OrderSummaryProjection on every placed order, Inventory's on an unreserved despatch — so a service with no projection shows nothing here. It only ever measures a read model this service feeds from its own domain events (§7.5); one fed by another service's contract never touches the outbox and stays empty here.

panels.title: Commands the domain refused
panels.description: command.domain_rejected (§9.8). Feeds no SLO row — a business signal that happens to share the meter, and it belongs on a dashboard rather than on a pager. The `error` tag is an Error.Code and never a cancellation reason: a payment-declined cancellation is a command the domain ACCEPTED.

panels.title: Work a worker keeps in its own tables — what delivery lag cannot see
Notifications waiting, by step
panels.description: notifications.waiting — Pending rows past their first backoff, by the step they wait on: order_record, contact or relay. Delivery lag stops when a consumer starts, and Notifications' consumers only write a row, so this is the send worker's wait that the panel above cannot see. Every replica reads the same table, so the series are combined with max, not sum. A rise on relay during an outage is the breaker parking the queue of rows, not a fault; docs/runbooks/queue-backlog.md says how to read each step.

panels.title: Notifications overdue — the send worker's capacity
panels.description: notifications.overdue — how long Pending rows due for a pass have gone unclaimed past two ticks, in shipping.shipments.overdue's form. The waiting gauge beside it counts only rows a pass has already backed off, so a row no pass has reached is visible here alone. Healthy, it stays near zero; one that climbs with the relay and Keycloak answering is too few replicas, and the fix is replicaCount in deploy/helm/notifications/values.yaml (§15.3).

panels.title: Projection — an order nobody can see
Oldest order with no owner (alert: UnattributedOrders)
panels.description: bff.orders.unattributed (ADR-051): how long the oldest row in the BFF's order projection has waited for an Ordering event to name its buyer. §10.7 returns such a row to nobody, so above zero for long means a buyer's history is missing an order. Seconds is ordinary — a payment or shipment event beat OrderPlaced. Empty is not zero: a failed read is an absent series. Runbook: docs/runbooks/unattributed-order.md.
